newsitem.title: GERMANY: Text of German government statement on reserves.
newsitem.headline: Text of German government statement on reserves.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government made the following statement on Wednesday in response to the Bundesbank's criticism of its plan to revalue the central bank's gold and currency reserves.

The statement was issued by Kohl, Finance Minister Theo Waigel, Free Democratic Party (FDP) chairman Wolfgang Gerhardt and parliamentary leaders Wolfgang Schaeuble of Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU), Hermann Otto Solms (FDP) and Michael Glos of Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU).
The statement has been translated into English by Reuters.

"In preparation for the third phase of the European economic and monetary union, the coalition intends to revalue the currency reserves of the Bundesbank according to the principles developed by the European Monetary Institute. But the currency reserves will in no way be sold.
The successful stability policies of the Bundesbank as well as its sole responsibility for monetary policy will not in any way be hampered by the planned adjustments of the currency reserves.

The coalition agrees with the Bundesbank that the independence of the central bank is of preeminent importance for the stability of the deutschemark and the euro. The credibility stemming from the independence of the German Bundesbank will be strengthened by the planned adjustment of the Bundesbank law to the even stricter rules of the European System of Central Banks.

The coalition and the Bundesbank council agree that a revaluation of the currency reserves will be necessary according to the planned accounting rules of the European System of Central Banks. The Bundesbank's tasks will change on entry into the European Monetary Union.

The financial solidity of the Bundesbank will be completely protected through the cautious revaluation. Even today the gold reserves in most European central banks are already valued much higher than they are at the Bundesbank.
The change in currency reserves resulting from the revalutation will take place with complete respect for the monetary policy tasks of the German Bundesbank.

The coalition stresses its view that this necessary adjustment should not wait until 1999. Rather it is reasonable and also responsible to carry out this adjustment now and start with the planned transfer of the resulting financial means to the Inherited Debt Redemption Fund in 1997.

The step-by-step transfer to the Inherited Debt Redemption Fund enables the Bundesbank to compensate for the liquidity effect resulting from the revaluation by controlling the money supply. This is not an intervention in the independent monetary policy of the Bundesbank.
The coalition will strive to include the revaluation of the reserves into the current legislative process."
